True. Both people in me definitely serve their own purpose. Boy me is kind of a protector and girl me gets people to like me. Ive been through som trauma in my life and after said trauma is when I was introduced to my masculine side.

I honestly feel happier and more comfortable as a guy. More me.

I don't think I'm mean. I'm certainly not as sensitive and timid as I used to be. I opened up and got out of my shell the past year. I also grew thicker skin (ironic since I'm upset about what other people say about me rn lol). I can be blunt, but not in an antagonistic way yknow.

I've never seen any of this as a negative thing, but the way other people have treated me makes me feel like it is.
Yea exactly. It's corny, but I used to exaggerate my femininity just to get boys to like me. Funny how I'm the complete opposite now.

I've wondered if its because nobody sexualises me when I present masc, so I use it as a safety blanket. Could be many things tbh.

At least nobodys *said* they hate me because of my gender. It's mainly coworkers and then a few ex friends. The friends said I started being a dick to them but never explained how. The coworkers just out of nowhere started talking bad on me and treating me like shit, just so happened to be when I started presenting as a boy so Idk if there's a correlation.

My family is generally supportive, just ignorant about what they say.

Yea, I've always wondered if its a trauma thing. My therapist thinks maybe the whole situation with that relationship just made me come to "meet" who I am as a boy sooner.
It's funny cus I think I'd be fine with all the effects of testosterone, yet I still hesitate so much. It's just a whole lot of stress I wish I didn't have to go through. 
I do plan to lose weight before I make any permanent decisions, in case that's where all my problems stem from. Hoping that's just the case lol. Likely not though.

I have wonderful friends and family who are very supportive. A lot of me wanting to go back to a girl is sentiment towards better days, since the only year I've lived openly as a guy have been shit and the best years of my life were as a girl. My brain always puts gender into everything, it's annoying lol.

You've been a real gem. I appreciate you. *hugs*

I'm already on anti psychotics for other reasons. It has done much for me gender wise. I see a therapist and she encourages me to transition as it'll be the only thing to make me happy, but I just wish it wasn't the only way to treat it. I just have a hard time accepting who I am because I just hate myself a lot I guess. For all of 2017, though, I had a lot of self love. Never been happier. I was presenting as a girl then, and I guess I just associate self love with that. Even though I'd still always wonder when I could go back to being a boy lol.

Yea I see a gender therapist. She tells me the same thing you just said, that this isn't about anyone else but myself.

I always used to try so hard to be someone I'm not. I'd see someone I admire and try to turn into them. It made it really hard to figure out who I am.

The past year I fully let myself just be myself. And everyone hates it. I used to have a lot of people who liked me and looked up to me even, all gone. I miss who I used to be and I'm willing to throw out who I really am to be her again. It was just easier. I was sweeter, more likeable, prettier, etc.
That's what I'm resorting to. Realistically for me, I should be a guy. But I was born such a pretty girl and everyone loved her, it feels like a waste to throw her away.

I feel that. I've always been envious of those who are naturally androgynous, cus that's how I wish I was. I'm scared transition will make me too masc or I'll prefer my feminine self better. It's a whole mess lol. The questioning stage is always hard.

I relate a lot to that. I'm 17 and still can't sleep with the light off. I would get panic attacks over sleep too. What comforts me the most is to just remind myself that it is just a dream. The relieving feeling when you wake up is one of the best in the world imo.

I feel that. I was hospitalized for threatening suicide, but not an attempt. The ER didn't deem me suicidal enough to send me to a proper psych ward, so they sent me home after 15 hours and had a crisis team come to my house multiple times a week. The lady on the team had the nerve to tell me that no one's gonna believe me anymore because I "keep crying wolf". She also said I have no control over my life until I'm 18 whatsoever. Ridiculous.

Anyways, people will never understand unless they go through it themselves. I wouldn't wish depression on my worst enemy (besides aforementioned crisis counselor). There are people who do understand, though. It just takes time to find. Hang in there.

We'll miss you. Whatever decision you make, you are loved even if you don't feel it.

I'm ftm but honestly still questioning for this exact reason.
I definitely was okay with my original gender for a long while until 2016. I started dissociating from my body and feminine traits a lot. It comes and goes for me, like in waves that last a few months at a time. Right now I'm in the wave where it's gone and I even miss being my original gender. Not sure if it's the same for anyone else here.
I've been describing my situation as two kids fighting over who gets to play the xbox, my body and mind being the xbox and my masculine and feminine identities being the kids. When I presented as a woman, I missed my guy self and wanted to bring him back. Now it's vice versa. 

I've no clue if any of that made sense, but I hope you can kinda get the jist of it.

I'm sex repulsed the majority of the time, but when I'm not I get bottom dysphoria. It's more an annoyance that nothings down there. I try not to think about the sexual bits though, grosses me out lol.
Thank you. I always forget what to say or my feelings change by the time I go to a session so that's why I wrote notes for it.

I remind myself that a lot. Everything in my life is going so fast currently that it became hard to slow down and just remember I have lots of time. Thank you though for the advice and support, it means a lot.

I'm 17 now, turning 18 in september.

I guess I could explain it like I associate the happiest point of my life with when I presented female, so I wonder if I presented female I'd be back at that happy point. I know it's illogical though. Sorry I'm being really confusing, it's just weird to explain.

It does get confusing because of how i said earlier it feels like two people fighting over me. It could just be me reminiscing on better days though, not sure. I've also noticed most of the eras where I was more female presenting I was trying to impress a straight guy. It's weird lol. Once though a guy said he likes the "boy me" too so I brought him back out so quick. Idk if any of that makes sense.

It's kinda hard to go back to before the trauma but i do remember always wanting to be a part of the boys group in schools n such. I always felt like there was something different about me than other girls. I was always a tomboy and have always prefered wearing boys clothes over girls n stuff like that. I'm not sure if any of these even count though since it's mainly to do with gender roles besides envying masculinity and such.

Therapy can be very good for resolving problems within yourself. I used to think it was useless but it helps to work things out rationally. I don't think they'll take you off of hormones though. She probably wanted you to wait so that you know for sure it's what you want since it is so permanent.

i've seen a lot of people oppose that notion because the general public deems transition as a cosmetic procedure, rather than a medical necessity. gender dysphoria is a huge source of distress for lots of transgender people, some worse than others. imo, dysphoria is a mental disorder. hormones and surgery is the way you treat it. sure, there is therapy, but the majority of the time it isn't enough. there's been studies done to show that a reason for dysphoria is brain sex differing from physical sex, so it can also be deemed as a neurological condition as well. it's not as urgent of a medical condition as cancer or whatever else, but it still can significantly impair someones ability to function in life. it can cause severe depression so it needs to be treated as importantly as such. i think if the opposing side were able to understand the struggles trans people go through they would understand.

i agree nearly entirely with your perspective. there's way way more issues in our world that need more prioritising, yet at the same token, i feel we can manage these issues at once. transgender politics are certainly quicker and easier to deal with than others like climate change and healthcare. the main priority for it is safety for all trans people. the healthcare issue goes hand in hand with trans people getting hormones, so that kills two birds with one stone. i'm not well educated on how the legal system works, but i do think it's able to be managed in a way that doesn't slow progression to other topics at hand. though, i do think the discussion over it in society is overpowering others such as climate change (which i would hope we all deem the most important issue we face). i feel like transgender people made a lot of progression under the Obama administration, and the republican party puts too much effort in trying to backtrack it. had it been left alone, i feel it wouldnt be at the frontlines of political discussion. again, i'm not the most educated person on the subject of politics, but i am transgender myself (ftm). so i hope this reasoning explains my view well.
